# nish/net/static

Serves the files under one directory through `nish/net/http-server` (HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 over TLS and cleartext, HTTP/3) or through `nish/net/handler` (HTTP/1.1), with a content type per extension, an ETag and a Last-Modified, a single byte range, and a path check that refuses to leave the directory.

```ts
import {
  STATIC_NOT_FOUND,
  StaticFiles,
  StaticLimits,
  staticContentType,
} from "nish/net/static";
```

<scalar-code-group>

```ts example.ts
import { HANDLER_SENT } from "nish/net/handler"
import { STATIC_NOT_FOUND, StaticFiles, StaticLimits } from "nish/net/static"

const ASSETS: i32 = 0
router.add("GET", "/assets/*")
router.add("HEAD", "/assets/*")
const files = new StaticFiles("./public", new StaticLimits())
// per request:
case ASSETS: {
  const sent: i32 = files.serve(server, r, r.paramStart(0), r.paramEnd(0))
  if (sent === STATIC_NOT_FOUND) server.empty(r, 404)
}
```

</scalar-code-group>

<scalar-detail title="The path is the program's span, decoded and checked">

`serve` takes a
`[start, end)` span of the request's head, the rest of the path a `*`
route gave, percent-decodes it strictly (`%00` and a bad escape are
refused) and splits it on `/`. A segment that is empty (`a//b`), `.`, `..`
or any other name that starts with a dot, or that holds a backslash or a
control byte, refuses the whole path. What is left is joined under the
root and resolved with `realpathSync`, and a result that is not the root's
own real path or under it is refused too, so a symbolic link that leads
out is not followed out. A refused path answers `STATIC_NOT_FOUND` with
`refused` set; the program answers it, as it answers a missing file.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="The cache follows the disk">

Each file of at most
`StaticLimits.maxCachedBytes` is kept in one of `maxEntries` slots, keyed
by its decoded path and its coding; every request stats the file again, and
a slot whose modification time or size differs is read again before it is
sent. A larger file is read from disk for each request, a chunk at a time.
Nothing is cached by URL, and no response is cached.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="A precompressed sibling is sent when it is asked for">

With
`precompressed` on, a request whose `Accept-Encoding` offers `br` or `gzip`
is sent `name.br` or `name.gz` when that file exists beside `name`, with a
`Content-Encoding`, the base name's content type and an ETag of its own.
Codings are weighed by their q-values; a tie goes to `br`, then `gzip`,
then the file as it is. With it on, every file it sends, and every 304,
says `Vary: Accept-Encoding`.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="Validators and ranges">

The ETag is strong, `"<size>-<mtime µs>"` in
hex, with `-br` or `-gz` for a coded variant. `If-None-Match` (weak
comparison, or `*`) answers 304; without it, an `If-Modified-Since` in the
IMF-fixdate form at or after the file's second answers 304, and another
date form is ignored. One `bytes=` range answers 206 with its
`Content-Range`; more than one sends the whole file; a malformed or
unsatisfiable one answers 416. `If-Range` keeps the range only for an
equal strong ETag, or the exact Last-Modified date of a file unchanged
for a second or more. A range on a coded variant counts the coded bytes.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="What it reaches">

`fs.read` for the files under the root and `clock`
for their modification times; `--sandbox --allow fs.read=<root>` holds
the reads to the directory. The record is `docs/security/static.md`.

</scalar-detail>

## Classes

### StaticFiles

Serves the files under one directory; one per server, not reentrant.

```ts
class StaticFiles
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new StaticFiles(root: string, limits: StaticLimits)` | A server of the files under `root`, which is resolved once, now. Limits out of range (`maxEntries` or `maxPath` outside 1 to 4096, or a `maxCachedBytes` outside 0 to 2^30) leave the root empty, so every GET or HEAD is not found. |
| `refused: boolean` | Whether the last `serve` that answered `STATIC_NOT_FOUND` refused the path rather than missing the file. |
| `root: string` | The root's real path, or `""` when it did not resolve (then every request is not found). |
| `status: i32` | The status the last `serve` sent, or 0 when it sent none. |
| `serve(server: HttpServer, r: HttpServerRequest, pathStart: i32, pathEnd: i32): i32` | Serves the file `r`'s head names at `[pathStart, pathEnd)`, a path relative to the root (one leading `/` is dropped), through `server`. |
| `serveHandler(h: HttpHandler, r: HttpRequest, pathStart: i32, pathEnd: i32): i32` | `serve` through `nish/net/handler`'s HTTP/1.1 carrier. |
| `tryServeHandler(h: HttpHandler, r: HttpRequest, pathStart: i32, pathEnd: i32): Result<i32, string>` | `serveHandler` through the handler's `try` calls: a misuse that makes `start`, `write` or `end` panic comes back as the handler's reason instead, with the file closed; so does a field index the handler gives no value span for, before anything is sent. |

### StaticLimits

What `StaticFiles` holds and reads.

```ts
class StaticLimits
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new StaticLimits()` |  |
| `index: boolean` | Whether an empty path, or one that ends in `/`, serves `index.html` there. |
| `maxCachedBytes: i32` | The largest file the cache keeps, at most 2^30; a larger one is read from disk on each request. |
| `maxEntries: i32` | How many files the cache keeps at once. |
| `maxPath: i32` | The longest path span `serve` takes, before decoding; a longer one is refused. |
| `precompressed: boolean` | Whether a `name.br` or `name.gz` beside `name` is sent when `Accept-Encoding` offers it. |

## Constants

<scalar-card title="-30" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`STATIC_NOT_FOUND: i32`

What `serve` answers when it sent nothing: the file is missing or not a regular file, or the path was refused (`refused`).

</scalar-card>
